item.title: Free SDoL winter sports physical — Tue Nov 10, 3:15 PM
item.description:
SDoL provides free physicals to student-athletes prior to the start of competition each sports season. Any student who is in grade 7 through 12 who plan to participate in a sport during the year must have a physical. When appropriate, transportation is provided to the site where physicals are offered. Student-athletes must bring a signed copy of the PIAA Physical Form (download below). Sections 1-5 must be completed fully. We will accept walk-ins until 6:30 p.m., but those with an appointment will be given priority. 3:15 p.m. – 5:00 p.m. @ McCaskey High School – East Buses are available for all SDoL students wanting to play a sport during the school year. For the bus schedule, download the flyer below. Click here to download flyer (English) | Español SIGN UP HERE

item.description:
The School District of Lancaster is inviting community members to become part of Valued Volunteers – Together We Read, a districtwide initiative that connects volunteers with students to help strengthen reading skills. The training serves as both the district’s required Valued Volunteers orientation and a kickoff for the Together We Read initiative. Participants will learn about the volunteer process while also receiving reading strategies, tips, and resources they can use when reading with students in our schools. item.title: The social signal - a color coded social mixer — Fri Nov 13, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Meet People Lancaster STOP LIGHT PARTIES ARE BACK!!! But with a twist.
Your attire won’t reflect your current relationship status for this party. Your color is tied to your social comfort level and battery life for meeting new people. It signals your openness to be approached.
Social club events can feel pretty intimidating. You scan the room and people are engaged in conversations. You don’t know which conversation you can join without “interrupting”. Now you’re self conscious about how long you’re just standing in the corner. Your mind goes blank on what to even say, so you hide in the bathroom until you can work up the courage to come back out and approach someone.
What do you do at this party if you experience any of these things? YOU APPROACH A GREEN!

item.description:
Vespers, Sunday evenings at 5:00 PM | In person only A contemplative candlelit service to nurture mind, body and spirit Join us Sunday evenings for Vespers, a warm and inviting weekly gathering in the serene surroundings of the Saint James Chapel. This quiet, reflective service embraces Christianity’s rich prayer traditions and the embodied practices that nurture our spiritual lives today. Gather with us for uplifting singing, find solace in moments of silence, and choose the posture that feels most comfortable as we open our hearts to listen for God’s voice and center ourselves for the week ahead. item.title: Evening Compline — Sun Nov 15, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Dillsburg Game Night - Calvary Methodist Church in the Family Center — Wed Nov 18, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Central PA Game Club Dillsburg Game Night meets every Wednesday from 6:30-9:30pm for casual tabletop games. We’ve been going strong since 2016, and most Wednesdays you’ll find about 30-40 gamers who love to learn and teach new games. It’s a great group of friendly people.
Given the timeframe, most of the games played are light to medium Euros, although many of us also love card games (including trick-taking games) and party games. We have a library of about 200 games available to play, and people typically bring their own games as well.
We also run long game days (typically every other month, usually a Saturday 2-9pm) and other special events. Join us on Facebook or Discord for more information about those.
Attendees do not often RSVP on Meetup. It may show 1 person is coming but we have 40 people every Wednesday and will cancel the event if it is not happening. Feel free to message with questions.
Cost: Free Who: All Ages (15 and under must be accompanied by an adult) When: Every

item.title: Holiday Grief Workshop — Sat Dec 5, 10:00 AM — Church of the Apostles UCC
item.description:
💙 The holidays can be a difficult time when you’re grieving or learning to navigate life after a loss. This December, our Inclusive Church focus is grief during the holidays, and we’re making space for those feelings with a special Holiday Grief Workshop led by Grief & After-Loss Mentor Megan Malick. 🕯️ During this two-hour workshop, you’ll create your own 5 Senses First Aid Kit, using sight, sound, scent, touch, and taste to help ground your nervous system and find moments of comfort when grief feels overwhelming. 📅 Saturday, December 5, from 10 AM–12 PM at COA. 💲 Cost: $25 per person (covers workshop materials). 🎟️ Register through Realm, by calling or emailing the church office, or online by Clicking Here 💚 Scholarships are available to help cover the cost if needed. Please speak with Rev. Kathryn Kuhn for more information.
Source: Church of the Apostles UCC

item.description:
Being One Center in Lancaster County Life can be frustrating and distressing! Sometimes we just feel overwhelmed, insecure, or lost!
The good news is, you're not alone!
We warmly invite you to check-in and connect with community in our Online Spiritual Support Group. In each meeting, we will discuss our current stressors and see how we can positively cope using our spiritual tools to overcome these challenges.
Together we can help each other grow and expand our consciousness for these high vibrational times.
Donations Greatly Appreciated!
This Event is lovingly hosted By Anna Bojczuk. Anna is a Registered nurse with over 40 years of experience as well as a gifted Energy worker. Anna is also long-time volunteer and inspiration in the Being One Center Community.
Donations to the Being One Center are greatly appreciated (https://www.paypal.com/donate?token=AzIxMnj72R-pxLPP0cGQILM7OPiZs5zbsOdxGA7LFH60Wkr_0YcLATVAkIHYVjrFl4PP36X2GkDEJbaM)

Whether it is a book group, a Bible study, or a discussion group, we seek to offer diverse offerings to grow deeper in our faith through community and encouragement from each other.
Women’s Gathering is a lay-led group that explores topics related to faith and spiritual practices and periodically seeks outside sources and opportunities to deepen their experience. item.title: Children's Chapel — Sun Nov 15, 10:30 AM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Disposable Humanity Screening and Q&A — Tue Nov 17, 7:00 PM — Ware Center for the Arts
item.description:
Join us at the Ware Center for a free screening of the film Disposable Humanity—plus a community discussion panel and a Q&A with the filmmakers.
The Mitchell family—esteemed Disability Studies scholars and filmmakers—delve into the chilling legacy of the Nazi Aktion T4 program. This investigative documentary recounts the long-obscured history of how over 300,000 disabled individuals became the initial victims of the Third Reich. Targeted by the T4 program as having a “life unworthy of living,” their murders laid the groundwork for the Holocaust that followed. 6:15 PM • Pre-show community panel discussion Post-show • Q&A with director Cameron S. Mitchell Co-presented by the MU Disability Film Festival and Congregation Shaarai Shomayim.

item.title: C. Emlen Urban & The Chocolate King — Thu Nov 19, 5:30 PM — LancasterHistory Museum & Research Center
item.description:
One built an empire with a Kiss and the other designed it. This is the untold story of Milton S. Hershey and his architect, C. Emlen Urban. What drove these two men to achieve goals and fame beyond their wildest dreams? Why is one an American icon and the other unknown beyond his hometown? Drawn from his new book, Urban and the Chocolate King, architect and historian Gregg Scott joins LancasterHistory to tell the tale of two men who met as young boys in the small town of Lancaster, PA, and began a journey of design and construction that endured for fifty years.
Gregg Scott is a Fellow of the American Institute of Architects, a partner emeritus and co-founder of RLPS Architects, a monthly columnist for LNP, and twice recipient of the Journalist and Educators Award presented by the Historic Preservation Trust of Lancaster County. Most recently, the author of Urban Legend, Urban Alphabet, and the 2026 fall release of Urban and the Chocolate King.
Learn More
